title: Plaice and celery fishcakes with apple slaw

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, fish, celery, apples, breadcrumbs, yoghurt and mustard are all ordinary home kitchen foods.

supermarket.reason: Plaice fillets and everything else are stocked by mainstream supermarkets at everyday prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: A lidded pan, frying pan and masher are ordinary kit, and shaping and frying fishcakes is within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 400g fish to 800g potato makes eight sensible cakes for four, and pressing damp mash straight into crumbs holds well enough without an egg wash.

honest_times.reason: Forty minutes of active work covers peeling, shaping, crumbing, frying in batches and slicing the slaw, and the 20 minutes of cooking matches the boiling and steaming.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Six celery sticks run through both the cakes and the apple slaw, which suits a late November dinner.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fish, potato and a fresh celery and apple slaw make a proper family dinner.
